# Finch Therapeutics (FNCH): Cash Burn, Runway, and Strategic Position at the Takeda Inflection Point (Mid-2022)

## 1. Executive Summary

As of June 30, 2022, Finch Therapeutics reported **$104.7 million in cash and cash equivalents** (down from $133.5 million at December 31, 2021) and guided that this balance — supplemented by expected sublease income on its newly leased office/lab space — would fund operations only **"into the first quarter of 2024"** (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R2.htm; https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/takeda-returns-two-assets-back-finchs-nest-deciding-migrate-solo; https://www.geneonline.com/takeda-walks-away-from-microbiome-deal-with-finch/). That guidance implied a monthly burn of roughly **$5.0 million** — a figure that already excluded near-term Takeda milestones because of Takeda's pending pipeline review. Eight days after the Q2 2022 earnings disclosure, Takeda formally terminated the collaboration for convenience (notice August 19, 2022; effective November 17, 2022), eliminating Finch's only partnership revenue stream and up to ~$176–354 million in potential milestone payments. The intersection of a ~21-month runway, a hostile biotech financing market, and the loss of the sole partnership converted Finch's situation from a growth-funding problem into an endgame: successive restructurings (20% in April 2022, 37% in September 2022, ~95% in January 2023), abandonment of the clinical pipeline, and a pivot to IP monetization via licensing and litigation against Ferring/Rebiotix. The analysis below shows the burn math, explains why the runway calculation was more fragile than it appeared, and identifies the strategic risks the timeline created for the IP-monetization strategy.

## 2. Implied Monthly Cash Burn Rate: Calculation

**Inputs (Q2 2022 Form 10-Q, filed August 11, 2022):**
- Cash and cash equivalents, June 30, 2022: **$104.673 million** (December 31, 2021: $133.481 million) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R2.htm)
- Non-current restricted cash: $2.568 million (excluded from usable liquidity)
- Runway guidance: "into the first quarter of 2024," i.e., through approximately March 31, 2024 (https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/takeda-returns-two-assets-back-finchs-nest-deciding-migrate-solo)

**Calculation:**
- July 1, 2022 → March 31, 2024 = 6 months (H2 2022) + 12 months (2023) + 3 months (Q1 2024) = **21 months**
- Implied burn = $104.673M ÷ 21 = **$4.98 million/month (~$59.8 million/year)**
- Sensitivity: if "into Q1 2024" means only through January 2024 (19 months), burn = $5.51M/month; through February 2024 (20 months), $5.23M/month; if runway were only through December 31, 2023 (18 months), $5.82M/month. **Reasonable range: ~$4.8–5.8 million/month; central estimate ~$5.0 million/month.**

**Benchmark against actual pre-guidance burn:**
- H1 2022 net cash used in operating activities: **$41.485 million** → $6.91M/month; adding investing outflows ($1.803M of capex), total cash consumption was ~$7.2M/month (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R7.htm)
- Q2 2022 GAAP operating expenses of $22.99M annualize to **~$92 million** — nearly the entire cash balance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R4.htm)

The implied ~$5.0M/month plan therefore embedded a **~28–38% reduction in cash burn** versus the H1 2022 actual pace. Three levers were expected to deliver this: (1) the September 1, 2022 restructuring — a 37% workforce cut (50 FTEs) with ~$1.6 million in one-time severance costs, approved August 30, 2022 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022018005/fnch-20220901.htm); (2) suspension of the IND-ready FIN-211 (autism) Phase 1 initiation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022018005/fnch-ex99_1.htm); and (3) sublease income offsetting a large new lease commitment — Finch added a $37.1 million right-of-use asset in H1 2022 (ROU assets rose from $5.1M to $41.2M), with H1 2022 operating lease cash payments of $4.6 million (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R7.htm). Note also that the runway was calculated **after** a $14.6 million term loan raised in H1 2022 (loan payable, non-current: $14,620K; net borrowing proceeds $14,738K), meaning debt capacity had already been partially tapped (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R2.htm; R7.htm).

**Reality check on the plan:** Q3 2022 cash fell to $85.3 million — a ~$19.4 million one-quarter decline (~$6.5M/month), well above the implied plan (https://medcitynews.com/2023/01/gut-punch-finchs-flagging-microbiome-program-folds-leading-to-95-staff-cut/). This overshoot forced the January 2023 decision to discontinue the PRISM4 Phase 3 trial of CP101 in recurrent C. difficile and cut ~95% of staff. FY2023 operating cash use was $31.5 million (~$2.6M/month) and cash ended 2023 at $25.1 million; Finch entered Q1 2024 — the original runway endpoint — with $20.8 million only because it had shrunk to an IP-holding shell (SEC EDGAR XBRL, CIK 1733257, FY2023 10-Q/10-K data; Q1 2024 10-Q). In short, the ~$5M/month plan was not achievable while retaining clinical programs; only near-total retrenchment made the timeline survivable.

## 3. Collaboration Revenue Trends and Opex Structure During the Partnership Transition

**Revenue collapse:** Total revenue fell from $6.383 million in H1 2021 to **$0.715 million in H1 2022** (−89%), with Q2 2022 revenue of just $361K (−87% YoY) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R4.htm). The decline traces to the August 2021 amendment under which Takeda assumed primary responsibility for TAK-524 development and manufacturing, winding down Finch's reimbursed R&D activity; by 2023 revenue was $107K and zero in 2024 (SEC EDGAR XBRL, CIK 1733257).

**Why the revenue decline overstated the cash impact — but the milestone loss did not:** Most Takeda revenue was reimbursement of R&D costs Finch itself incurred, so when Takeda took over development, roughly offsetting revenue and cost reductions moved off Finch's P&L (H1 2022 R&D of $29.5M was only +9% YoY despite the transition). The true cash damage was prospective: the collaboration carried up to **$354 million in total potential payments per candidate**, of which ~$176–180 million in milestones remained available as of 2021, against only **>$44 million actually received** ($10M upfront + $4M milestones + >$30M R&D reimbursement) (https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/finch-takeda-end-ibd-microbiome-drug-deal/630592/; https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/takeda-returns-two-assets-back-finchs-nest-deciding-migrate-solo; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022017792/fnch-20220819.htm). The runway guidance already assumed **zero** near-term Takeda milestone cash — management explicitly removed these from its runway analysis in the Q2 2022 earnings disclosure because of Takeda's pipeline review (https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/takeda-returns-two-assets-back-finchs-nest-deciding-migrate-solo).

**Opex structure and fixed-cost rigidity:** H1 2022 opex of $47.9M comprised R&D $29.5M (61%), G&A $17.6M (37%), and restructuring $0.9M. G&A grew **+68% YoY** (from $10.4M), reflecting public-company overhead plus the newly filed Ferring/Rebiotix litigation (December 2021) — a fixed legal drag that would become the dominant cash outflow in the IP-monetization era. The new headquarters lease added a rigid multi-year commitment precisely as revenue evaporated, making the sublease plan essential to the runway math. Net loss for H1 2022 was $47.3M against $104.7M of cash — the company was consuming ~45% of its liquidity every six months at the pre-restructuring pace (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022016637/R4.htm).

## 4. Takeda's TAK-524 Program Review: Impact on Financing Urgency and Negotiating Position

**Escalating urgency.** The Q2 2022 10-Q/earnings (August 11, 2022) disclosed that Takeda was reviewing its pipeline and that Finch had stripped near-term milestones from its runway analysis — a clear signal management viewed partnership cash as unreliable. Takeda's termination-for-convenience notice followed on August 19, effective November 17, 2022, returning worldwide rights to FIN-524 (ex-TAK-524), FIN-525, and all IBD microbiome candidates (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022017792/fnch-20220819.htm). This converted an uncertainty into a certain loss of the company's only external funding source. With ~21 months of runway at ~$5M/month, Finch had roughly a two-to-three-quarter window to secure alternative capital on acceptable terms; instead, CEO Mark Smith cited the "current capital market environment" as a driver of the 37% workforce cut announced September 1, 2022 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022018005/fnch-ex99_1.htm). By year-end 2022, Finch received a Nasdaq notice for trading below the $1.00 minimum, closing off conventional equity financing (https://medcitynews.com/2023/01/gut-punch-finchs-flagging-microbiome-program-folds-leading-to-95-staff-cut/).

**Weakened negotiating position.** Three dynamics compounded:
1. **Distress signaling.** Two layoff rounds in five months (20% in April 2022 after the FDA's March 2022 clinical hold on CP101; 37% in September 2022) advertised Finch's constraints to any counterparty (https://endpoints.news/one-week-after-takeda-walks-away-finch-faces-second-round-of-layoffs-pipeline-pruning/; https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/finch-layoff-takeda-microbiome-restructuring/631141/).
2. **Unattractive assets in a cooling sector.** The returned FIN-524/FIN-525 assets were preclinical, and Takeda — the most informed possible partner, having taken over TAK-524 development in August 2021 — walked away for convenience after ~$44M invested. Takeda simultaneously terminated its Nubiyota collaboration, signaling a portfolio-wide exit from microbiome R&D rather than a verdict on Finch alone (https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/finch-takeda-end-ibd-microbiome-drug-deal/630592/). Prospective partners could wait out Finch's cash exhaustion.
3. **No leverage over Takeda.** Termination for convenience was contractually permitted with 90 days' notice; Finch's public posture was limited to "exploring collaboration opportunities" for the returned assets (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017022017792/fnch-ex99_1.htm).

**One offsetting benefit:** the termination returned worldwide IBD rights unencumbered by Takeda's exclusive license, simplifying ownership of the IP estate for future licensing or enforcement — a modest positive for the monetization strategy that followed, though with preclinical-stage assets and no development funding, Finch's bargaining power remained minimal.

## 5. Strategic Risks to the IP Monetization Strategy and Operational Flexibility

The January 2023 pivot was explicit: discontinue PRISM4 Phase 3, cut ~95% of staff, and "shift strategic focus towards realizing the value of our intellectual property estate" — 113+ issued U.S. and foreign patents — through licensing and enforcement (https://medcitynews.com/2023/01/gut-punch-finchs-flagging-microbiome-program-folds-leading-to-95-staff-cut/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000095017024035952/fnch-20231231.htm). The mid-2022 timeline created five structural risks:

1. **Sequencing mismatch between runway and monetization timelines.** The Q1 2024 runway was shorter than any realistic litigation or licensing payoff. The Ferring/Rebiotix trial (filed December 2021 as a declaratory-judgment action; Finch/UMN counterclaimed) did not reach verdict until **August 9, 2024** — roughly five months *after* the original runway endpoint — with appeals expected to extend into 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000119312524198362/d801504d8k.htm; https://dockets.justia.com/docket/circuit-courts/cafc/26-2055). Survival to monetization required near-total operational liquidation, betting the company on a single docket.
2. **Partial and contested litigation recovery.** The jury found willful infringement but invalidated one claim each from the '309 and '080 patents, awarding a $25.0M upfront payment plus $0.815M in running royalties on Rebyota sales through trial — well below Finch's expert's $50M-upfront/30%-royalty theory — with post-trial motions, enhanced-damages requests, ongoing-royalty claims, and appeal all pending (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733257/000119312524198362/d801504d8k.htm; https://www.ded.uscourts.gov/sites/ded/files/opinions/21-1694.pdf; https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/finch-wins-us-jury-trial-against-ferring-over-fecal-transplant-patents-2024-08-09/).

# Fortive's Portfolio Strategy After the Precision Technologies (Ralliant) Separation: Segment Economics, Momentum, and Positioning

## 1. Executive Summary

Fortive completed the spin-off of its Precision Technologies (PT) segment as Ralliant Corporation (NYSE: RAL) on June 28, 2025, distributing one Ralliant share per three Fortive shares (~113 million shares) and receiving $1.15 billion in cash consideration from Ralliant (~$1.0 billion net of ~$150 million unremitted cash) ([Fortive 8-K, June 30, 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916625000104/ex991-pressrelease.htm); [Pro forma 8-K EX-99.2](https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000104/ex992-unauditedproformasta.htm)). The segment-level data show the spin removed Fortive's **slowest-growing, most cyclically deteriorating, and margin-compressing segment**, leaving a two-segment company anchored by Intelligent Operating Solutions (IOS) — the clear unit-economics leader — with Advanced Healthcare Solutions (AHS) as the fastest-improving margin-recovery story. The Q1 2025 vs. Q1 2024 consolidated margin decline (-400 bps GAAP) was almost entirely a PT phenomenon, validating the divestment logic, and the first post-spin quarter (Q3 2025) delivered margin expansion in both retained segments.

## 2. Q2 2025 Segment Operating Margins vs. FY2024 Full-Year Margins

**Q2 2025 (as reported in the 10-Q, three months ended June 27, 2025 — the final quarter including PT):** ([Q2 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916625000120/ftv-20250627.htm))

| Segment | Q2-25 Revenue | Q2-25 Op. Profit | **Q2-25 Op. Margin** | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intelligent Operating Solutions | $675.7M | $166.7M | **24.7%** | 166.7 ÷ 675.7 = 24.67% |
| Precision Technologies | $523.6M | $93.2M | **17.8%** | 93.2 ÷ 523.6 = 17.80% |
| Advanced Healthcare Solutions | $319.5M | $39.1M | **12.2%** | 39.1 ÷ 319.5 = 12.24% |
| **Total** | $1,518.8M | $222.2M | **14.6%** | incl. -$76.8M unallocated "Other" |

**FY2024 full-year (as reported in the 2024 10-K):** ([10-K MD&A](https://grepcent.com/company/FTV/mda/fy2024/); [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916625000024/ftv-20241231.htm))

| Segment | FY24 Revenue | FY24 Op. Profit | **FY24 Op. Margin** | FY23 Margin | Δ YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IOS | $2,714.7M | $704.6M | **26.0%** (25.95%) | 24.1% | +190 bps |
| PT | $2,229.4M | $500.0M | **22.4%** (22.43%) | 24.5% | -210 bps |
| AHS | $1,287.7M | $155.6M | **12.1%** (12.08%) | 8.3% | +380 bps |

**Comparison and interpretation:**

- **IOS** ran at 24.7% in Q2-25 vs. a 26.0% FY24 average (-1.3 pp). This gap is largely seasonal/period-specific, not structural: Q2-24 was also below the FY24 average (25.6% vs. 26.0%), and Q2-25 absorbed tariff headwinds. On the company's continuing-operations presentation (PT treated as discontinued), IOS earned a **24.5% GAAP operating margin ($171M/$697M) with a 33.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY** ([Q2-25 press release](https://investors.fortive.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/271/fortive-reports-second-quarter-2025-results)).
- **AHS** at 12.2% in Q2-25 was *at or slightly above* its FY24 full-year average (12.1%) — and up YoY on the continuing-ops basis (11.2% vs. 11.0%, +20 bps), with adjusted EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 26.9% and adjusted gross margin improving to just over 59% from just under 58% ([Q2-25 earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/07/30/fortive-ftv-q2-2025-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- **PT** at 17.8% in Q2-25 sat **4.6 pp below** its FY24 average (22.4%) — and that FY24 average was itself down 210 bps from 2023. PT's Q2-25 revenue fell 5.1% YoY ($523.6M vs. $551.8M) and its operating profit fell 19.2% ($93.2M vs. $115.3M).

**Strongest unit economics: IOS, unambiguously** — roughly double AHS's GAAP margin and ~7 pp above PT in Q2-25, with the highest adjusted EBITDA margins (33.8% in Q2-25; 34.6% in Q3-25). **Strongest trajectory: AHS** — +380 bps in FY2024 (the largest expansion of any segment), margins holding up through the difficult Q2 and then expanding 150 bps YoY to 12.9% in Q3-25. PT had the weakest economics *and* the worst trajectory: a 210 bps FY24 decline driven by -145 bps of EA-acquisition deal costs, -320 bps from acquired-business amortization/fair-value adjustments, and volume declines, only partly offset by a +285 bps property-sale gain ([10-K MD&A](https://grepcent.com/company/FTV/mda/fy2024/)).

*Measurement note:* the press-release "continuing operations" segment figures (IOS $697M revenue/24.5% margin; AHS $320M/11.2%) differ modestly from the 10-Q as-reported figures because the press release treats PT as discontinued operations for both periods; both presentations support the same conclusions. On the recast basis in the 2025 10-K, FY2024 continuing-ops margins were IOS 25.3% ($708.0M/$2,793.2M) and AHS 10.8% ($138.5M/$1,287.7M) ([2025 10-K segment note](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916626000007/R42.htm)) — the IOS-vs-AHS hierarchy is unchanged.

## 3. Revenue Momentum: 2023 → 2024

| Segment | FY2023 Revenue | FY2024 Revenue | **Reported Growth** | Core Growth (non-GAAP) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IOS | $2,612.2M | $2,714.7M | **+3.9%** | +3.4% |
| PT | $2,223.7M | $2,229.4M | **+0.3%** | **-3.7%** |
| AHS | $1,229.4M | $1,287.7M | **+4.7%** | **+6.1%** |
| Total | $6,065.3M | $6,231.8M | +2.7% | +1.3% |

Calculations: IOS (2,714.7/2,612.2 − 1) = +3.92%; PT (2,229.4/2,223.7 − 1) = +0.26%; AHS (1,287.7/1,229.4 − 1) = +4.74%.

The momentum pattern is stark: **PT's flat reported growth masked a 3.7% organic decline**, propped up by the $1.72 billion EA Elektro-Automatik acquisition (+4.4 pp contribution, net of the Invetech divestiture). PT's decline was broad-based — mid-single-digit declines in developed markets, low-double-digit declines in China, and volume reductions in test & measurement and industrial sensing. **AHS was the organic growth leader (+6.1% core)** on pricing plus sterilization and dosimetry volume; IOS grew +3.4% core on pricing, gas detection, and facility/asset-lifecycle SaaS ([10-K MD&A](https://grepcent.com/company/FTV/mda/fy2024/)). The segment Fortive chose to spin was precisely the one with negative organic momentum and contracting margins; the two retained segments combined for positive core growth and margin expansion.

## 4. Q1 2025 vs. Q1 2024: Where the Consolidated Margin Erosion Came From

([Q1 2025 8-K EX-99.1](https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000079/q12025-ex991.htm))

| Metric | Q1-25 | Q1-24 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $1,474.2M | $1,524.5M | -3.3% (core -2%) |
| GAAP operating profit | $233.6M | $302.2M | -22.7% |
| **GAAP operating margin** | **15.8%** | **19.8%** | **-400 bps** |
| Adjusted operating margin | 25.3% | ~25.1% | **+

- Q1-25 vs Q1-24 consolidated margin decline (-400bps) was concentrated in PT; retained segments were resilient (IOS +122bps; adj op margin +20bps company-wide). This reveals the strategic logic: the drag was in the divested unit.

# Options Framework for a $700 Account Targeting $200–300/Week
**Educational framework only — not personalized financial advice. Options can lose 100% of invested premium; the target below is mathematically extreme and most retail options traders lose money.**

---

## 0. The Reality Check (read first)

The target implies a weekly return of **28.6%–42.9% on a $700 account** ($200/$700 and $300/$700). Compounded for 52 weeks, $200/week grows $700 into ~$331 million; $300/week into ~$79 billion. No sustainable strategy produces this. The framework below is therefore best read as: *the rules you'd need to follow, and the (very demanding) win-rate math the target requires* — with the honest conclusion that the target is only plausible in short bursts, not reliably, and that a realistic goal for this account size is $30–$150/week with strict risk control.

---

## 1. Position-Sizing Rules and Maximum Risk per Trade

Standard guidance for small accounts is to risk **1–5% of account value per trade** (tastylive research cited by TradingPilot; OptionsPilot recommends 3–5% for accounts under $10K because 1–2% is too small to fit any real options position). On $700:

| Risk level | Max loss per trade |
|---|---|
| 2% (conservative textbook) | $14 — unusable for options |
| 5% | **$35** |
| 7% | **$49** |
| 10% (aggressive ceiling) | **$70** |

**Rules:**
- **Max risk per trade: $35–$70 (5–10% of account).** Below $35/trade, almost no liquid option structure fits; above $70, five straight losses cut the account ~41%.
- **Max 3 open positions; portfolio heat ≤ 20–25%** of account at risk across all positions (Ainvest/OptionPilot caps total portfolio risk at 10–15% for larger accounts; a small account must run slightly hotter to trade at all).
- **One position per underlying; no correlated pairs** (e.g., don't hold bullish spreads on two chip stocks simultaneously — count them as one risk unit).
- **Contracts = floor(Max risk ÷ max loss per contract).** If one contract's max loss exceeds the budget, narrow the strikes or skip the trade — never "round up."
- **No undefined-risk positions** (naked calls/puts, strangles). Max loss must be knowable before entry (Optionstrading.org's core 1%-rule caveat).
- **Keep ≥ 30% ($210) in cash** as a reserve for losses and flexibility.
- **Stop-trading rule:** after 2 consecutive max losses in a week, stop for the week (−$100 to −$140 max weekly damage).

---

## 2. Permitted Strategies (all defined-risk)

| Strategy | Use case | Typical structure here |
|---|---|---|
| **Single-leg long call/put** | High-conviction directional move, catalyst-driven | Premium ≤ $70/contract (i.e., ≤ $0.70) |
| **Bull call / bear put debit spread** | Directional with cheaper breakeven | $1–$2.50 wide |
| **Bull put / bear call credit spread** | Directional-with-cushion or range fade | $1–$2 wide, credit ≥ 25–33% of width |
| **Long call/put debit spread as earnings bet** | Pre-event, IV-aware | Only if IV crush risk is acceptable |

**Prohibited:** naked shorts, strangles/straddles (undefined risk), calendars/diagonals (leg risk and spread cost too high at this size), far-OTM lottery weeklies, and any position held through earnings unless that *is* the thesis with ≤ $35 at risk.

Rationale: verticals cap both sides, so max loss is known pre-entry — the precondition for any percent-risk sizing rule to work (Optionstrading.org; EMPEERYAL). Debit spreads lower the breakeven vs. a lone long option; credit spreads give a statistical cushion but invert the reward:risk (Moontower; OptionSamurai).

---

## 3. Stock Selection Criteria (Technicals)

Universe: large-cap, high-dollar-volume names and major ETFs (SPY, QQQ, AAPL, NVDA, TSLA, MSFT, AMZN class) — average 20-day dollar volume ≥ $20M (GitHub stock-scanner filter), because liquidity lives there.

**Bullish checklist (all must pass):**
1. **Trend:** price above rising 20-day EMA, and 20-EMA above 50-EMA (full bullish alignment — Stoptions scoring model).
2. **Momentum zone:** RSI(14) between **50–70** — strong but not exhausted (Stoptions uses 55–70; >70 is overbought per Stocks365). For fade setups, RSI >75 with a reversal candle.
3. **Location:** price within **5% of a defined support zone** (pivot-low cluster) and ≥ 5% below the next resistance (scanner filter #4/#5) — so the required move has room and the stop level is objective.
4. **Volume confirmation:** breakout/pullback day volume ≥ **1.5× the 20-day average** (scanner filter #6; Optionstranglers).
5. **Volatility:** ATR ≥ ~2% of price — the stock must actually move for a 3–21 day option to pay (scanner volatility flag).
6. **No binary events inside the hold window** (earnings, FDA, Fed) unless the trade is explicitly an event bet.

Bearish setups mirror this (below falling 20-EMA, RSI 30–50 or >75 rolling over, price near resistance).

Honest caveat: RSI + MA checklists are the default retail screen and are not sufficient by themselves (Quant-Builder) — they define *where* to look, not a proven edge.

---

## 4. Strike and Expiry Selection (3–21 Day Holds)

**Expiry:**
- **Debit spreads / long options: 14–30 DTE**, plan to exit in 3–10 days — avoids the final-week theta burn.
- **Credit spreads: 7–14 DTE**, hold toward expiry or close at 50–70% of max profit.
- Never hold a long option into its final 3 days unless it's already a winner.

**Strikes:**
- **Expected move first:** the ATM straddle ≈ expected move. For a 14-day, 35% IV stock at $47.80, that's ~$2.61 (±5.5%) — computed via Black-Scholes below. **Breakeven must sit inside the expected move** (OptionEV's "breakeven feasibility" test). If the stock must move 8% but the expected move is 5%, skip it.
- **Debit spreads:** buy the ~0.40–0.45 delta strike, sell the strike at/near the expected-move target or the next resistance. Width $1–$2.50. Pay ≤ ~35% of width.
- **Credit spreads:** short strike at the ~0.25–0.30 delta (≈ 1 expected-move away), long strike $1–$2 further. Credit ≥ 25–33% of width.
- **Single-leg:** ATM or slightly ITM (0.50–0.55 delta); avoid far-OTM weeklies (ApexVol's "avoid" list).

**Management:** take profits at **50% of max profit** (TradeAlgo: raises realized win rate ~10–15% and shortens duration); cut losses at 50% of premium paid for long options, or 2× credit received for credit spreads; no averaging down; no rolling without a fresh thesis.

---

## 5. Liquidity Filters

Per OptionVisualizer, ApexVol, OptionsKing, and Baruffa's screen (converging conventions):

| Filter | Minimum / Maximum |
|---|---|
| **Open interest** | ≥ 500 contracts at *both* strikes (1,000+ preferred; hard floor 100) |
| **Daily option volume** | ≥ 100 contracts (≥ 25 acceptable late-day pulse check) |
| **Bid-ask spread** | ≤ 10% of mid (≤ 5% for the most-traded names); **absolute cap $0.05–$0.10** on cheap options |
| **Underlying** | S&P 500 / mega-cap / major ETF only; no small caps |
| **Quote sanity** | Mid-price fills only; if the spread is > $0.05 on a sub-$1 option, use limit orders and walk away if unfilled |

The spread is the one cost you pay twice (entry and exit) — a 15% spread on a $0.60 option is 9¢ each way, ~30% round-trip drag (OptionsKing). Entries are optional; exits are not (Optionscanner).

---

## 6. Example Trade A — Bull Call Debit Spread (hypothetical)

**Setup:** "XYZ" at **$47.80**, above rising 20/50 EMAs, RSI 58, pulled back to support at $46.50 on 1.8× volume, no earnings for 25 days. 14-day expected move ≈ ±$2.61 (±5.5%) at 35% IV.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Structure | Buy 1 XYZ **$48 call**, sell 1 XYZ **$50 call** (bull call spread) |
| Expiry | 14 DTE (weekly) |
| Entry (net debit) | **$0.70** ($70 per spread) — near the BS fair value of $0.70 at 35% IV |
| Position size | 1 contract = $70 = **10% of account** (max risk tier) |
| Max loss | **$70** (below $48 at expiry) |
| Max profit | $130 (spread worth $2.00 above $50) |
| Breakeven | **$48.70** (inside the ±$2.61 expected move ✓) |
| Target | Exit at $1.20–$1.40 (+$50 to +$70) or hold to $1.30 max target |
| Liquidity | OI 1,200/900; volume 850/610; spread $0.69/$0.71 ✓ |

**P/L at expiry (1 contract):**

| XYZ price | Spread value | P/L |
|---|---|---|
| $44.00 | $0.00 | **−$70** (max loss) |
| $47.00 | $0.00 | −$70 |
| $47.80 (entry) | $0.00 | −$70 |
| $48.70 | $0.70 | $0 (breakeven) |
| $49.50 | $1.50 | **+$80** |
| $50.00+ | $2.00 | **+$130** (max profit) |

**Probabilities (Black-Scholes, 35% IV, 14 DTE):** P(above $48) ≈ 46%; P(above breakeven $48.70) ≈ **38%**; P(max profit, above $50) ≈ **24.5%**. Rough EV at market prices ≈ −$3 — i.e., the *market* prices this as fair; any positive expectancy must come from your technical read being better than the market's, which is the entire challenge.

---

## 7. Example Trade B — Bear Call Credit Spread (hypothetical)

**Setup:** "ABC" at **$49.20**, RSI 76 rolling over, rejected at resistance $50.00 three times, below-falling 20-EMA day on 2.1× volume. 7-day expected move ≈ ±$2.17 (±4.4%) at 40% IV.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Structure | Sell 1 ABC **$50 call**, buy 1 ABC **$51 call** (bear call spread) |
| Expiry | 7 DTE |
| Entry (net credit) | **$0.32** ($32 collected) — near BS fair value $0.31 |
| Position size | 1 contract; max loss $68 = **9.7% of account** |
| Max profit | **$32** (ABC ≤ $50 at expiry) |
| Max loss | **$68** (ABC ≥ $51) |
| Breakeven | **$50.32** |
| Target | Close at $0.10–$0.16 (50–70% of credit) = +$16 to +$22 |
| Liquidity | OI 2,400/1,800; volume 1,100/740; spread $0.31/$0.33 ✓ |

**P/L at expiry (1 contract):**

| ABC price | Spread value | P/L |
|---|---|---|
| $47.00 | $0.00 | **+$32** (max profit) |
| $49.20 (entry) | $0.00 | +$32 |
| $50.00 | $0.00 | +$32 |
| $50.32 | $0.32 | $0 (breakeven) |
| $50.50 | $0.50 | −$18 |
| $51.00+ | $1.00 | **−$68** (max loss) |

**Probabilities:** P(ABC > $50) ≈ 37.5%; P(above breakeven $50.32) ≈ 33% → **POP ≈ 67%**. But EV at market prices ≈ −$1.30: the 67% win rate is exactly compensated by the 2.1:1 loss:win ratio. High win rate ≠ positive expectancy.

---

## 8. Win Rate and Probability Distribution Required for $200–300/Week

With per-trade risk **R**, average win **W×R**, and **n** trades/week, the win rate needed to clear $250/week is:

**p = (250/n + R) / (R × (W + 1))**

| Trades/week | Risk/trade | Avg win | Required win rate for $250/wk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | $70 | 2.0R | **73%** |
| 5 | $70 | 2.0R | **57%** |
| 5 | $70 | 1.5R | **69%** |
| 7 | $70 | 2.0R | **50%** |
| 7 | $35 | 2.0R | **67%** |
| 10 | $70 | 2.0R | **45%** |
| 10 | $35 | 2.0R | **57%** |
| 3 | $35 | 2.0R | 113% — **impossible** |
| 5 | $35 | 1.5R | 97% — effectively impossible |

**The workable envelope:** ~5–10 trades/week, $70 risk each (10% of account), average winner ≥ 1.5–2× risk, win rate **50–60%**. For example: 5 trades/week, 55% win rate, 1.6R average winner → EV ≈ $30/trade → **~$150/week** — half the target. Hitting $250/week needs the top of every range simultaneously: 60% win rate, 2R winners, 5–7 trades, zero slippage leakage.

**Distribution reality:**
- A 55%-win-rate trader still has a **1.8% chance of 5 straight losses** and a ~0.2% chance of 8 straight; at 10% risk per trade, 5 straight losses = **−41% drawdown** ($700 → ~$410). Recovery then requires +70%.
- The credit-spread profile (67% win rate, 0.47R wins, 1R losses) needs ~**80%+ realized win rate** to clear $250/week at this size — above its own theoretical POP, i.e., negative expectancy.
- **Conclusion:** the required distribution is roughly *binomial with p ≈ 0.55, n ≈ 5–7, payoff 2:1* — a distribution that skilled, disciplined traders occasionally achieve for short stretches and that fees, slippage, and variance erode for nearly everyone. The $200–300/week target on $700 is a ~29–43% weekly return; the defensible version of this framework targets **$30–$150/week (4–21%)** while the account compounds, and treats any $200+ week as an outlier, not a plan.

**Sources:** position sizing — optionstrading.org/blog/one-percent-rule-options-trading/, optionspilot.app/blog/how-to-size-options-trades-small-accounts, tradingpilot.com/blog/small-account-options-trading, optionpilot.ainvest.com/guides/options-risk-management-guide, empeeryal.com/blog/position-sizing-options-risk; liquidity — optionvisualizer.com/documentation/workflows/liquidity-screening, apexvol.com/learn/options-liquidity, optionsking.app/learn/options-liquidity-screening.html, fabiobaruffa.com/articles/options-liquidity-market-execution-python/, optionscanner.ai/learn/options-liquidity-screening; technicals — optionstranglers.com.sg/blogs/news/building-a-technical-toolkit-for-options-trading, stoptions.ai/blog/how-momentum-scanning-works-sp500-options, stocks365.com/blog/rsi-in-options-trading-master-momentum-for-perfect-timing, github.com/NadirAliOfficial/stock-scanner-bot; probabilities/management — tradealgo.com/trading-guides/options/options-profit-calculator-guide, optionev.com/technical-ev-analyzer, optionsamurai.com/blog/creating-an-optimum-vertical-spread/, moontower.substack.com/p/a-deeper-understanding-of-vertical.
